changed_in.5.2: A function written in C is written into rather than passed over: the values it was created holding can be replaced, and an empty name comes back to say which one. Earlier versions answer nothing for any function written in C and write nothing. A Lua function that mentions a global also begins carrying the table it reads global names out of as a captured variable called `_ENV`, which is what makes this the call that hands a loaded chunk a different set of globals after the fact; earlier versions keep that table elsewhere and it is not among a function's upvalues.
changed_in.5.3: An index carrying a fraction is refused rather than being cut down to a whole number, and so is one too large to hold an exact whole-number value.
